found.location: ## Meet the persona you made, step 3
found.issue: stale-claim. Step 3 read `Say hello.`, which tells the reader to speak first. The product speaks first: once the voice is ready the client sends MEET_KICKOFF silently (desktop-client/src/components/setup/Interview.tsx:28-30 and 118) and the new persona greets the reader unprompted. The **Second brain setup** button in step 4 does not exist until that greeting finishes, because it renders only while `met` is true and `met` is set on speaking_complete after the handoff (Interview.tsx:194-197, 319, 413-424). wiki/features/personas.md:69 already states they greet you first, so the how-to also contradicted its own concept page.
found.fix: Rewrite step 3 as listening and replying rather than initiating, and add a result note that the **Second brain setup** button appears once they have finished speaking.
found.reason: The reader is told to act at the one moment the product acts for them, and is not told when the control that leaves this screen appears. A reader who types into a composer that is about to be interrupted, or who looks for a button that is not rendered yet, thinks setup has stalled.

found.location: ## Before you start, third bullet, and ## Work through the rest with him
found.issue: The page pressed finality twice (`It happens once`, `the interview is over for good`) and never stated that the persona itself can be changed afterwards. wiki/features/personas.md:156-162 says a persona you made is not fixed: who they are, how they speak, what they may do, and their prompt are all editable on the Personas page, with a candidate voice audible before committing. Nothing on this page carried that fact or linked to it.
found.fix: Add one result note after the color and name paragraph in ## Work through the rest with him pointing at features/personas.md#changing-a-persona-later.
found.reason: The reader makes five irreversible-sounding choices in a few minutes. Believing a voice or color is permanent is what makes someone stall on a question, answer defensively, or reinstall to try again.

detailed_review.score_reasoning: One spine applied twice. Baseline: the page starts at 10 and every baseline finding subtracts. F1 (step 3 tells the reader to speak first when the product speaks first, and step 4's button does not exist yet) 1, F2 (the handover screen is described and not shown, while the page's two other screen sections both carry figures) 1, F3 (the page presses finality and never says the persona is editable afterwards) 1, F4 (shipped screen copy notated two ways) 0.5. Sum 3.5, so score_before = floor(10 - 3.5) = 6, NEEDS_WORK. After: all four were fixed in this run and moved to changed[]. The single regrade pass turned up two new items, F5 (lowercase accent tokens, 0.5) and F6 (no answer for an interrupted setup, 1), both open in remaining[]. Sum 1.5, so score_after = floor(10 - 1.5) = 8, PASS with minor nits open. Delta +2. Two notes for a human reading this number. First, F6 existed at baseline and I did not find it until the regrade; the append-only rule means it counts against the after score and not the before score, which makes the delta smaller than it would otherwise be, not larger. Had I found it at baseline the page would have opened at 5. Second, the cap at 9 for a non-empty remaining[] never bound here, because the detraction math already lands below it. No shell was available, so the linter was read rather than run and the page was checked against its rules by hand; that is stated in the `linter` field rather than reported as a command I did not execute.
detailed_review.what_worked: F1 is the fix that matters. The handover is the emotional peak of first run and the one stretch where nothing is asked of the reader, and the page was telling them to act. It now says the persona speaks first, unprompted, as soon as the voice is ready, invites a reply rather than requiring one, and says the Second brain setup button appears once they have finished. That also removes a contradiction with wiki/features/personas.md:69, which already told readers they are greeted first. F3 answers the question the page's own framing provokes: five choices arrive in about four exchanges and the page twice says this happens once, so a reader needs to know, at the moment they are choosing, that the persona is editable afterwards. F2 gives the capture queue the third screen; the page now requests a figure for every surface it asks a reader to recognize. F4 is small but real: the reader can now see that the trailing period belongs to the screen title. Everything else on the page held up under fact-checking, and that is worth saying plainly, because this page was written from source rather than from a stale record. The four opening options, the five swatches, the ten accents, the two-to-four attribute rule, the ninety-second voice wait, both pills, the disabled Go to the house button, the three exits from the second-brain beat, and the case-insensitive name collision all match the tree. The page correctly documents the swatches the handler accepts (Plum) rather than the ones the schema advertises (Heather), which is the T44 defect, and it prints no tool schema, so it does not inherit the `voice_id` error that T43 owns on wiki/first-run.md. On the source disagreement the dispatch asked me to settle: SetupFlow is right and the comment is stale. desktop-client/src/components/setup/SetupFlow.tsx:350 wires the Interview's onDone to setStep('second-brain'), and the SecondBrain screen's own onDone at line 353 is the one that calls onExit(true). The comment at Interview.tsx:414-416 saying the button opens the house describes an earlier cut. The author's resolution was correct, and the code comment is what should change.
detailed_review.what_holds_score_down: F6, at 1, is the larger of the two open items and the only one with real reader weight. The page tells you twice that this happens once and never tells you what happens if you have to stop. The source does not settle it either: SetupFlow.tsx:76-79 says an unfinished setup leaves the completed flag false and the next launch comes back to setup, but the step state initializes at `welcome`, so whether the reader lands back in the interview, at the start of setup, or in the install path is a question for a running house rather than for a file. Guessing it onto the page, or softening the finality language until the question stops arising, are both worse than leaving it open, so it is a blocked row rather than an edit. F5, at 0.5, is cosmetic: ten lowercase nationality adjectives in running prose read as a typo next to the capitalized `British accent` a few lines above. Outside the score, two things about this page's situation are worse than anything in its prose. Nothing in the corpus links to it: wiki/installing.md:142-147, wiki/getting-started.md:53-60 and wiki/clients/macos.md:130-131 all still send readers to First run for this walkthrough, and wiki/_index.md carries no entry. Those belong to T9, T7, T6 and T11, and this page cannot fix them. A page nobody can reach is not scored here, because the score grades the document, but it is the single biggest thing standing between this work and a reader.
